title: Hierarchical workload matrix and deterministic synthetic seed suite for CI perf gates
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Our CI perf gates and golden baselines are brittle for mixed workloads (chat, single-turn, long prefill+decode) and do not exercise combined kernel/attention scheduling edge cases. This causes intermittent regressions after kernel routing or prefill-scheduler changes because the current suites lack hierarchical coverage and deterministic seeds that reproduce KV-cache and attention boundary conditions.

Goal: Build a hierarchical workload matrix plus a deterministic synthetic-seed generator that produces stable, reproducible traces across models and hardware configurations to strengthen CI perf gates and make golden baselines robust. The suite must capture: short-turn chat, multi-turn with prefix caching, long prefill-only workloads, decode-heavy streaming, and adversarial attention patterns (large past contexts + sparse attention matrices).

Approach: 1) Define a two-axis workload taxonomy (interaction shape: single/multi/prefill/decode vs attention pressure: low/medium/high/sparse). 2) Curate a small set of 'mosaic' seeds per cell generated by a deterministic RNG + canonical tokenizer state so runs are reproducible across CI workers and hosts. 3) Implement a lightweight harness that can: replay synthetic traces, inject KV/noise boundary events, toggle attention-block-fusion flags, and capture detailed kernel-routing traces for later analysis. 4) Integrate the suite into CI as a set of gated jobs with quantile latency checks and P95/P99 regression thresholds tied to golden baselines.

Success metrics: - Reduced flaky perf regressions in CI by 70% over the next quarter; - New suite increases kernel-routing coverage by >40% relative to current golden runs; - CI job runtime increase limited to <25% with opportunity to run a full-matrix nightly and a smoke subset on PRs.

Deliverables: - Hierarchical workload matrix definition (confluence doc) - Deterministic seed generator and seed catalog - Synthetic trace harness with toggles for attention and KV events - CI jobs (PR-smoke subset + nightly full matrix) - Dashboard visualizing per-seed latency and kernel routing coverage
acceptance_criteria: Workload matrix doc published in Confluence with examples for each cell
Seed catalog of at least 24 deterministic seeds covering all matrix cells
Harness capable of replaying traces and toggling attention-block-fusion and KV cache events
CI configured: PRs run a 6-seed smoke subset; nightly runs full matrix; perf gates check P95 and P99 against golden baselines
Dashboards show per-seed latency distributions and kernel selection heatmaps for 3 representative models

2025-01-15 - Diego: Prototype deterministic-seed generator checked in: github.com/redwood/runtime/seed-gen PR #412 (draft). Needs cross-platform RNG review for Windows CI workers.
2025-01-18 - Eng-Infra review: Prefer use of guest-local clock-independent RNG (HMAC-DRBG) to ensure cross-host determinism. Diego updated generator accordingly.
2025-01-20 - Perf: Early runs show attention-block-fusion flag flips create P99 spikes on A100 with long prefill; added additional seeds to stress sparse-attention boundary conditions.
2025-01-22 - PM review (Noah): Suggested smoke subset selection rules: choose seeds that maximize kernel-coverage delta vs baseline. Added rule to harness sampler.
2025-01-24 - QA: Identified a nondeterminism in tokenization when using model-specific custom tokens; mitigation: normalize tokenizer vocab ordering in seed payloads.
